findings.mechanism: 04-races-and-atomicity – increments of _hits/_misses are read‑modify‑write and not atomic under concurrent access, so cache hit/miss counters can lose updates.
findings.remediation: Wrap updates to _hits and _misses in a threading.Lock (or use atomic counters) so each increment is performed under mutual exclusion.
findings.arithmetic: With N concurrent cache‑hits, each _hits += 1 may be interleaved with another thread, losing at most one increment per pair. In the worst case half the increments are lost, so observed hits ∈ [⌈N/2⌉, N].

prediction.condition: 100 concurrent get calls, all cache hits

findings.mechanism: 04-races-and-atomicity – concurrent writes to the shared _entries dict can corrupt the dictionary or overwrite entries, causing missing cache entries.
findings.remediation: Guard all accesses to _entries (get, put, clear) with a single threading.Lock or replace the dict with a thread‑safe mapping.
findings.arithmetic: With N concurrent distinct puts, each write can race with another, potentially losing up to half of the entries. Observed entry count after the writes ∈ [⌈N/2⌉, N].

prediction.condition: 50 concurrent put calls of distinct queries followed by 50 gets for those queries

findings.mechanism: 04-races-and-atomicity – clear() mutates _entries and resets counters without synchronization; if it runs while get() is reading or writing, a request can miss a cached entry and trigger duplicate work.
findings.remediation: Acquire the same lock used for get/put before clearing the cache, ensuring no concurrent reads or writes during clear.
findings.arithmetic: If clear runs concurrently with M get calls for the same key, at least one get may observe the cache as empty, causing an extra origin fetch. Hence duplicate side‑effects ≥ 1.

prediction.condition: clear invoked while 20 concurrent get calls for the same query
